title: Venustiano Carranza's coded telegrams from Veracruz, May and June 1915 (CEHM-Carso Fondo CDLXXX 1.17.1 to 1.42.1): number and letter-pair ciphers read by Prabal Gupta

steps.what: The contributor transcribed the ten telegrams from the CEHM scans in two passes agreeing on 99.2% of 1,292 tokens, checking sample pages on the scan.

Count matching on Spanish next-letter counts opened the number telegrams (65% to 77% of tokens on the largest set of 758, 35% on the 199-token set) and gave the plan of the key; the letter telegrams came from a one-to-one solve on Spanish.

The decryption was read as Spanish military orders; the weekday word before the letter telegrams was taken to name the day's table; a blind reader named four of six strings Spanish and two shuffled strings noise.

The contributor checked Narváez's 2025 article in Historia Mexicana 75/2 in full: it does not print these tables and does not decipher these telegrams; his 2019 book, Ángel and Morales-Luna (2008), the fondo XXI key sheets and Obregón (1917) were not checked.

Project check: the number telegrams decrypted again with the contributor's start letters agree with his decryption file on 98.2% of 1,056 letters (a check that the file follows the key); a word-list test over 1,001 letters (the second page of 1.22.1 left out) puts 62.8% in listed words against a mean of 4.2% and a best of 22.5% for 300 random start-letter sets; the swapped coded letters of 1.29.1, 1.39.1 and 1.40.1 agree with his decryption file on all 244 coded letters (VERIFICATION.md). No scan compared.

validation.notes: The project's n-gram test needs a Spanish model of the period (lang/) and a controlled key family; a word-list test against 300 random start-letter sets was used instead (VERIFICATION.md); it is not the n-gram validation.

outcome.method_basis: Contributor's claim: the keys were found from the ciphertext alone, with no key sheet and no sibling decipherment, by count matching on Spanish next-letter counts and a one-to-one solve; the project verified that the keys decrypt the telegrams into Spanish and re-ran a word-list control, but did not repeat the search. Priority is open: the key family may be in print (Narváez 2019 and others not checked).

outcome.fraction_read_source: The contributor's count: 1,013 of 1,050 number tokens (96.5%) give the reading's letter as typed; the others are mostly the clerk's slips and overstruck digits repaired by sense and are counted as read here. The guessed name in 1.42.1 and the unsettled run in 1.22.1 are small; the project's own sequence match is 98.2% of 1,056 letters.

texts.label: Ten telegrams of Venustiano Carranza's headquarters, 17 May to 9 June 1915 (CEHM-Carso Fondo CDLXXX)
texts.summary: Orders of Carranza's headquarters at Veracruz, which the contributor places in the war against Villa: to Obregón, the line is being reinforced as far as Apam and the convoy there is to go on; to Pablo González, a general brings a million pesos in small bills; to Nuevo Laredo, ten thousand dollars go to the customs administrator for General Dávila and 200,000 cartridges of two calibres leave New York; to Elías in New York, buy 915 Lee rifles for the next day's steamer; to Arredondo in Washington, ask whether the American government will allow repairs to the steamer Progreso in New York and place 425 dollars with the consul in Havana.

reading_review.note: Read the decryption as Spanish telegram sentences: the coded stretches build coherent orders that join the clear words around them; the repairs of clerk's slips and the name Cosío Rovelo are the contributor's, and 1.32.1 is a weak reading of 21 letters.

prior.where: The CEHM cards give no content. Constitutionalist keys are known in print (Ángel and Morales-Luna 2008; Narváez 2025, which the contributor checked in full and found does not print these tables or decipher these telegrams); Narváez's 2019 book, the CEHM fondo XXI key sheets and Obregón (1917) were not checked.

human: Prabal Gupta transcribed the telegrams, ran the solvers and built the reading (issue #321, repository prabal-rje/branicki-1757). The project re-ran the decryptions and a control; it has not seen the scans.
